correctness.rationale: Let i index a minimal u_i=-a<0, m>0, p=(u+a1)/(m+a), hence L=mp and u-L=a(p-1). Since p_i=0, p>=0 and sum w p=1, concentration of weighted mass at the smallest remaining weight w_j yields ||u-L||_w^2 <= a^2(1-w_j)/w_j. For any feasible z, h=z-u has h_i>=a and sum w h=0; Cauchy-Schwarz on complementary coordinates yields ||h||_w^2 >= a^2 w_i/(1-w_i). The resulting bound is maximized at the two smallest weights. A single-negative-coordinate family with u_i=-epsilon and other small positive coordinates approaching zero concentrates p at j; the actual weighted orthogonal projection zeros i and shifts all other coordinates by a common offset, giving asymptotic equality. LGL endpoint weights 1/[N(N-1)] are minimal because |P_{N-1}(x)|<=1. For N=2 ratio=1. Independently verified near-sharp examples with weights (.05,.07,.18,.7), (.1,.1,.3,.5), (.3,.7), and LGL endpoints for N=2..10.

value.rationale: Distinguishes the exact and potentially quadratically large correction cost of a standard nodal positivity limiter from the least weighted Euclidean modification under identical conservation. It quantifies a real design tradeoff beyond the tautology that projections minimize distance, with degree-dependent sharpness for standard LGL discretizations. No claim about entropy or full PDE evolution.

final_claim: For any positive normalized quadrature weights, the sharp ratio of the weighted distance moved by mean-anchored radial positivity scaling to the minimum conservative nodally nonnegative weighted-l2 correction equals sqrt((1-w1)(1-w2)/(w1*w2)) for the two smallest weights; it is N(N-1)-1 for N-point Legendre-Gauss-Lobatto quadrature.
limitations: Static finite-dimensional scalar positivity with a single conserved weighted mean and the particular quadrature-weighted norm; no entropy constraints, full-element positivity, consistency of a time-marching method or bound on evolved PDE solution error. Full historical limiter-comparison manuscript unavailable.
